title: CDIF Version 1.1 Now Final
content:
After the initial release of the CDIF version 1.1 Profiles in June, and a subsequent round of testing and implementation, they have now been finalised. The release will henceforth be stable, with all further issues and features addressed in subsequent versions. The release can be found at https://book.cdif.org/ and https://github.com/Cross-Domain-Interoperability-Framework

Version 1.1 consists of profiles for JSON-LD implementation in support of cross-domain FAIR systems and applications:

Core (Schema.org) – basic general and administrative metadata
Discovery (Schema.org) – support for detailed cataloging and search
Concept Scheme (SKOS, OWL, XKOS) – Ontologies, glossaries, and other types of controlled vocabularies
Codelist (SKOS) – enumerated values for populating variables
Data Description (Schema.org/DDI-CDI) – describing data sets, including structural and physical information, plus links to semantics
Data Structure (DDI-CDI) – description of reusable data structures and variables
Manifest (RO Crate) – Packaging of related sets of metadata and data

title: From Checklists to Crisis Response: CODATA and UNESCO Present the First Global Survey on Data Policies for Times of Crisis
content:
Crises rarely wait for institutions to be ready for them. Floods, epidemics, earthquakes and displacement events unfold across borders, sectors and time zones, and the organisations that respond to them succeed or fail depending on whether they can find, trust and share the right data fast enough. That simple observation sits at the heart of the Data Policies for Times of Crisis (DPTC) Toolkit, developed jointly by UNESCO and the International Science Council’s Committee on Data (CODATA), and it was the common theme of two sessions to which CODATA contributed at the 2026 Global Conference of the International Decade of Sciences for Sustainable Development (IDSSD) in Paris: the ISC session on 16 July ‘Resilient Science for Resilient Societies: Protecting Knowledge and Scientists in Times of Crisis’, and the dedicated UNESCO–CODATA thematic session on 17 July ‘Data policies for times of crisis: Enabling open science for coordinated response’.

Two sessions, one message
